findings.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:461 awaits getCalendar inside an unawaited forEach, allowing Promise.all(apiDeletes) to run before recurring-booking updates are added and cancellation to finish without awaiting calendar synchronization.

packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125 and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts use async forEach callbacks without awaiting them, turning calendar-initialization exceptions into unhandled promise rejections that bypass the surrounding try/catch.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in both packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts and packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, the forEach callback is changed to 'async (bookingRef) => {...}' and uses 'await getCalendar(...)' inside. However, forEach does not await async callbacks - it fires them off and continues immediately. This means any exceptions thrown during the async operations (including the await getCalendar call) will result in unhandled promise rejections that bypass the surrounding try/catch block. This is a real bug introduced by the diff.
